question: Can repeatable AusTraits family-level phylogenetic-memory context be explained by family-specific tree geometry rather than biology?
population: The fixed 259-system, 42-family, 14-trait prospectively qualified AusTraits final core.

tree_metrics.n_tips: number of tips in the exact system tree
tree_metrics.polytomy_burden: 1 - Nnode/(n_tips-1); zero for a fully bifurcating rooted tree
tree_metrics.multifurcating_internal_fraction: fraction of internal parent nodes with out-degree >2
tree_metrics.pairwise_distance_cv: sd/mean of all unordered patristic distances
tree_metrics.pairwise_unique_fraction: number of exactly unique patristic-distance values divided by number of unordered pairs
tree_metrics.max_distance_tie_share: largest exact patristic-distance multiplicity divided by number of unordered pairs

analysis.primary_S3: rho ~ 0 + trait_name + standardized S3 tree metrics + (1|family), REML
analysis.mandatory_prune: same model using prune-only rho and prune tree metrics
analysis.comparison: compare adjusted family variance and conditional family repeatability with the already observed unadjusted values
analysis.one_at_a_time: also fit each geometry covariate separately to diagnose whether any single tree property absorbs the family effect

interpretation.family_effect_persists: Measured tree topology/distance geometry is not a simple explanation of lineage-wide context.
interpretation.family_effect_collapses: Treat family context as potentially generated by phylogenetic geometry rather than a biological lineage state.

hard_nonclaims: Persistence after these metrics does not prove a biological causal mechanism.
The residual component remains a mixture of biological system heterogeneity and estimation error.
Do not select or drop tree metrics based on their association with rho.
